claim: Earlier studies have shown that nephrons signal to each other, synchronize over short distances, and potentially form large synchronized clusters.
source: Earlier studies have shown that nephrons signal to each other, synchronize over short distances, and potentially form large synchronized clusters.
evidence: This claim is supported by references to prior research in the field, as indicated by the statement about 'earlier studies'.

claim: Large synchronized clusters would play an important role in renal autoregulation.
source: Such clusters would play an important role in renal autoregulation, but due to the technological limitations, their presence is yet to be confirmed.
evidence: This is a theoretical assertion based on understanding of renal physiology, presented as speculation about the functional role of synchronized clusters.

claim: Due to technological limitations, the presence of large synchronized clusters is yet to be confirmed.
source: Such clusters would play an important role in renal autoregulation, but due to the technological limitations, their presence is yet to be confirmed.
evidence: This statement acknowledges a gap in empirical evidence due to methodological constraints.

claim: The study introduces an approach for high-resolution laser speckle imaging of renal blood flow.
source: In the present study, we introduce an approach for high-resolution laser speckle imaging of renal blood flow and apply it to estimate the frequency and phase differences in rat kidney microcirculation under different conditions.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the methodological contribution of the study.

claim: The analysis unveiled the spatial and temporal evolution of synchronized blood flow clusters of various sizes, including the formation of large (>90 vessels) and long-lived clusters (>10 periods) locked at the frequency of the tubular glomerular feedback mechanism.
source: The analysis unveiled the spatial and temporal evolution of synchronized blood flow clusters of various sizes, including the formation of large (>90 vessels) and long-lived clusters (>10 periods) locked at the frequency of the tubular glomerular feedback mechanism.
evidence: This claim reports specific quantitative findings from the data analysis performed in the study.

claim: Infusion of vasoconstrictor angiotensin II promoted stronger synchronization.
source: Specifically, infusion of vasoconstrictor angiotensin II promoted stronger synchronization, while acetylcholine caused complete desynchronization.
evidence: This is a direct observation from experimental manipulation with angiotensin II.

claim: Acetylcholine caused complete desynchronization.
source: Specifically, infusion of vasoconstrictor angiotensin II promoted stronger synchronization, while acetylcholine caused complete desynchronization.
evidence: This is a direct observation from experimental manipulation with acetylcholine.

claim: The results confirm the presence of local synchronization in the renal microcirculatory blood flow.
source: The results confirm the presence of the local synchronization in the renal microcirculatory blood flow and that it changes depending on the condition of the vascular network and the blood pressure, which will have further implications for the role of such synchronization in pathologies development.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Synchronization changes depending on the condition of the vascular network and the blood pressure.
source: The results confirm the presence of the local synchronization in the renal microcirculatory blood flow and that it changes depending on the condition of the vascular network and the blood pressure, which will have further implications for the role of such synchronization in pathologies development.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental observations under different conditions (control, AngII, ACh).

claim: Two critical mechanisms in renal pressure autoregulation are the myogenic mechanism and tubuloglomerular feedback (TGF).
source: Based on measurements of tubule pressure responses to step changes in arterial pressure (Young and Marsh, 1981), vascular transfer functions (Chon et al., 1993; Chon et al., 2005; Cupples and Loutzenhiser, 1998; Marmarelis et al., 1999; Sakai et al., 1986; Shi et al., 2006), and renal blood flow response to arterial pressure forcing (Holstein-Rathlou et al., 1991), two critical mechanisms in renal pressure autoregulation, the myogenic mechanism and tubuloglomerular feedback (TGF), have emerged as the critical components.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research establishing these mechanisms.

claim: The myogenic mechanism operates at 5–10 s (0.1–0.2 Hz).
source: The two mechanisms operate at different time scales, generating spontaneous blood flow and pressure oscillations at different frequencies: 5–10 s (0.1–0.2 Hz) for the myogenic response and 30–50 s (0.02–0.033 Hz) for the TGF (Holstein-Rathlou and Marsh, 1989; Yip et al., 1993; Cupples and Loutzenhiser, 1998; Sosnovtseva et al., 2002; Just, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations documenting the temporal characteristics of the myogenic mechanism.

claim: The TGF mechanism operates at 30–50 s (0.02–0.033 Hz).
source: The two mechanisms operate at different time scales, generating spontaneous blood flow and pressure oscillations at different frequencies: 5–10 s (0.1–0.2 Hz) for the myogenic response and 30–50 s (0.02–0.033 Hz) for the TGF (Holstein-Rathlou and Marsh, 1989; Yip et al., 1993; Cupples and Loutzenhiser, 1998; Sosnovtseva et al., 2002; Just, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations documenting the temporal characteristics of TGF.

claim: Nephrons are linked via the renal vascular tree, which provides connections of different proximities.
source: Within a single kidney, all nephrons are linked via the renal vascular tree, which provides connections of different proximities - from few hundred microns for neighboring nephrons separated only by their respective afferent arterioles to nephrons only connected at the level of the renal artery, which plays a role of a single-supply source for all the nephrons.
evidence: This is a statement about the anatomical structure of the kidney based on established knowledge.

claim: Nephrons communicate via electrical signaling.
source: In addition to interaction through the blood flow and pressure, nephrons were found to communicate via electrical signaling (Marsh et al., 2019; Marsh et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies demonstrating electrical communication between nephrons.

claim: Adaptive synchronization across the renal microvascular network would increase the efficiency and dynamic range of autoregulation by engaging more preglomerular resistance.
source: Adaptive synchronization across the renal microvascular network would increase the efficiency and dynamic range of autoregulation by engaging more preglomerular resistance (Marsh et al., 2019; Zehra et al., 2021), preventing transmission of high systemic pressure to the glomeruli, which could lead to progressive glomerular and vascular injury.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and represents a theoretical understanding of the functional consequences of synchronization.

claim: Long-distance synchronization would argue strongly that renal autoregulation is a distributed process.
source: In addition, long-distance synchronization would argue strongly that renal autoregulation is a distributed process that can ensure an optimized oxygenation-perfusion matching and adjust to various internal or environmental conditions (Sosnovtseva et al., 2007; Mitrou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference about the implications of long-distance synchronization, supported by citations.

claim: Large-scale in-phase synchronization might become a mechanism leading to glomerular injury as it would substantially increase local pressure variation.
source: On the other hand, large-scale in-phase synchronization might become a mechanism leading to glomerular injury as it would substantially increase local pressure variation (Postnov et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to modeling work and represents a theoretical prediction.

claim: Micropuncture experiments showed that neighboring nephrons adjust their TGF-mediated tubular pressure oscillations to attain a synchronized regime.
source: Micropuncture experiments (Holstein-Rathlou, 1987; Källskog and Marsh, 1990; Yip et al., 1992; Sosnovtseva et al., 2007) showed that neighboring nephrons (originating from a common artery) adjust their TGF-mediated tubular pressure oscillations to attain a synchronized regime.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to micropuncture studies.

claim: Micropuncture experiments could only sample pairs or triplets of nephrons at any one time.
source: Although these experiments confirmed the existence of synchronization, only pairs or triplets of nephrons could be sampled at any one time.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of micropuncture methodology based on established knowledge.

claim: Laser speckle contrast imaging (LSCI) technology made assessment of co-operative efforts of a larger number of nephrons possible.
source: Assessment of co-operative efforts of a larger number of nephrons required a different approach and was made possible with laser speckle contrast imaging (LSCI) technology (Holstein-Rathlou et al., 2011; Mitrou et al., 2015; Scully et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies using LSCI for renal imaging.

claim: In LSCI, media with moving light scattering particles are illuminated with a near-infrared laser, and the backscattered light forms an interference pattern that appears more or less blurred depending on the speed of the particles.
source: In LSCI, media with moving light scattering particles, e.g., red blood cells, are illuminated with a near-infrared laser. The backscattered light, recorded by a camera, forms an interference pattern, which appears more or less blurred depending on the speed of the particles.
evidence: This is a description of the physical principles underlying LSCI technology.

claim: The LSCI pattern is analyzed to obtain qualitative maps of particle velocity and thus a blood flow estimate.
source: This pattern is then analysed to obtain qualitative maps of particle velocity and thus a blood flow estimate (Boas and Dunn, 2010; Briers et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations describing LSCI analysis methods.

claim: Holstein-Rathlou et al. first applied LSCI to map TGF oscillations over a large field of view.
source: First applied by Holstein-Rathlou et al. to map TGF oscillations over a large field of view, this method was later used to explore periodic activity in the myogenic frequency band (Scully et al., 2013; Mitrou et al., 2015), analyse spatial correlations in the renal blood flow (Brazhe et al., 2014), and study intrarenal drug distribution (Postnov et al., 2015a, Postnov et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a historical claim about the first application of LSCI to renal TGF mapping, supported by citation.

claim: Previous LSCI methods lacked resolution, both spatial and temporal, as well as signal-to-noise ratio, to convincingly confirm large-scale synchronization.
source: Although these results encouraged the large-scale synchronization hypothesis, the method lacked resolution, both spatial and temporal, as well as signal-to-noise ratio, to confirm it convincingly.
evidence: This is an assessment of the limitations of previous LSCI methods based on the authors' knowledge.

claim: The LSCI setup and data processing approach allow imaging renal microcirculation at 0.8 μm per pixel spatial resolution and imaging frequency to 160 Hz for 1024 × 1024 pixels.
source: Our LSCI setup and data processing approach allow imaging renal microcirculation at 0.8 μm per pixel spatial resolution and imaging frequency to 160 Hz for 1024 × 1024 pixels.
evidence: This is a specification of the technical capabilities of the imaging system developed in this study.

claim: Four vessels form two frequency-locked clusters (red-green and black-orange) that are synchronous most of the time.
source: From the corresponding dominant frequency and phase (Figure 1C and F), it can be seen that these vessels form two frequency-locked clusters (red-green and black-orange) that are synchronous most of the time.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of data shown in Figure 1, representing specific observations from the study.

claim: There are long periods when the two clusters synchronize, forming a larger cluster, interrupted with an asynchronous interval (from ≈850 to ≈1050 s).
source: Moreover, there are long periods when these clusters synchronize, forming a larger cluster, interrupted with an asynchronous interval (from ≈850 to ≈1050 s).
evidence: This is a specific observation from the time series data analysis.

claim: The improved spatial and temporal resolution allows recording BFI with less noise and better spatial localization.
source: As can be seen, the improved spatial and temporal resolution allows recording BFI with less noise and better spatial localization, e.g., identifying blood flow belonging to a single microcirculatory vessel.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison of data quality between old and new systems, as shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Averaged across all vessels blood flow index decreased by 17.3±2.3% in the vasoconstricted condition.
source: Averaged across all vessels blood flow index has decreased by 17.3±2.3% in the vasoconstricted condition and increased by 27.7±13.3% in the vasodilated condition.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data.

claim: Averaged across all vessels blood flow index increased by 27.7±13.3% in the vasodilated condition.
source: Averaged across all vessels blood flow index has decreased by 17.3±2.3% in the vasoconstricted condition and increased by 27.7±13.3% in the vasodilated condition.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data.

claim: During AngII infusion, vessels are significantly more likely to be synchronized with 20–50% of the field of view than in control or during ACh infusion.
source: From Figure 3, it can be seen that during AngII infusion, vessels are significantly more likely to be synchronized with 20–50% of the field of view than in control or during ACh infusion.
evidence: This claim is based on statistical analysis of the data shown in Figure 3.

claim: During ACh infusion, probability of a vessel being synchronized with less than 15% is significantly higher than during AngII infusion (p<0.05).
source: In the latter condition, probability of a vessel being synchronized with less than 15% is significantly higher than during AngII infusion (p<0.05).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the data analysis with reported p-value.

claim: The phase of oscillations within a cluster is space-dependent - it is mostly the same for the closely positioned vessels and gradually changes with distance.
source: Another distinct feature that we have observed is that the phase of oscillations within a cluster is space-dependent - it is mostly the same for the closely positioned vessels and gradually changes with distance.
evidence: This is an observation from the spatial analysis of phase data.

claim: The possibility of phase waves was previously hinted at in an earlier LSCI study where spatial correlations in renal blood flow were analyzed.
source: The possibility of such phase waves was previously hinted at in our earlier LSCI study, where spatial correlations in renal blood flow were analyzed (Brazhe et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim references prior work that suggested the existence of phase waves.

claim: This result is in good agreement with experimental micropuncture observations, where it is explained by the presence of fast electrical coupling acting over short distances.
source: This result is in good agreement with experimental micropuncture observations, where it is explained by the presence of fast electrical coupling acting over short distances.
evidence: This claim compares the current findings with prior micropuncture studies and their interpretation.

claim: AngII infusion increases anti-phase synchronization to 5%, showing a statistically significant difference with other conditions.
source: However, AngII infusion increases this number to 5%, showing a statistically significant difference with other conditions.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding with statistical significance from the phase difference analysis.

claim: Phase difference grows with distance.
source: Phase difference grows with distance, as can be seen from Figure 5B, reflecting the presence of phase waves.
evidence: This is an observation from the spatial analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In control and vasodilated conditions, phase change is relatively small (≈0.3 and 0.25 rad/mm).
source: While change is relatively small in the control and vasodilated conditions (≈0.3 and 0.25 rad/mm), it is strongly enhanced in the vasoconstricted condition, reaching, on average, ≈1 rad over 1 mm distance.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the spatial phase analysis.

claim: In the vasoconstricted condition, phase change is strongly enhanced, reaching on average ≈1 rad over 1 mm distance.
source: While change is relatively small in the control and vasodilated conditions (≈0.3 and 0.25 rad/mm), it is strongly enhanced in the vasoconstricted condition, reaching, on average, ≈1 rad over 1 mm distance.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the spatial phase analysis.

claim: Mathematical modeling showed that such phase difference can be explained by strengthened hemodynamic coupling, which increased vascular tone should cause.
source: As we showed with mathematical modeling (Postnov et al., 2012), such difference can be explained by strengthened hemodynamic coupling, which the increased vascular tone should cause.
evidence: This claim references prior modeling work to explain the observed phase differences.

claim: In the vasoconstricted condition, average synchronization duration reaches ≈40±13% of the observation time for neighboring vessels.
source: It is clear that synchronization is stronger in the vasoconstricted condition, with average duration reaching ≈40±13% of the observation time for neighboring vessels and gradually reducing to 24±6% for vessels located at more than 1 mm distance.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the synchronization duration analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: In the vasoconstricted condition, average synchronization duration gradually reduces to 24±6% for vessels located at more than 1 mm distance.
source: It is clear that synchronization is stronger in the vasoconstricted condition, with average duration reaching ≈40±13% of the observation time for neighboring vessels and gradually reducing to 24±6% for vessels located at more than 1 mm distance.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the synchronization duration analysis.

claim: In control, synchronization duration varies greatly but on average reduces with distance from ≈30% to ≈21%.
source: In control, synchronization duration varies greatly, but on average, it also reduces with distance, although at a slower rate than during AngII infusion—from ≈30% to ≈21%.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the synchronization duration analysis.

claim: During ACh infusion, synchronization duration is ≈15-13%, with only 2% reduction over 1mm of distance.
source: During the ACh infusion the synchronization duration is ≈15-13%, with only 2% reduction over 1mm of distance.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the synchronization duration analysis.

claim: Higher synchronization duration in control and during AngII infusion compared with ACh infusion suggests a long-distance nephron-to-nephron communication or a common driving force.
source: Higher synchronization duration in control and during AngII infusion compared with ACh infusion suggests a long-distance nephron-to-nephron communication or a common driving force.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of synchronization durations across conditions.

claim: The data confirm that blood flow in renal microcirculation tends to demonstrate clustered, frequency-locked activity.
source: Our data confirm that blood flow in renal microcirculation tends to demonstrate clustered, frequency-locked activity, with the clustering size and tendencies changing depending on the animal condition.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the experimental observations.

claim: Clustering size and tendencies change depending on the animal condition.
source: Our data confirm that blood flow in renal microcirculation tends to demonstrate clustered, frequency-locked activity, with the clustering size and tendencies changing depending on the animal condition.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from comparing results across different experimental conditions.

claim: A possible explanation for the stronger synchronization during the AngII infusion is stronger hemodynamic coupling due to increased vascular resistance.
source: A possible explanation for the stronger synchronization during the AngII infusion will be a stronger hemodynamic coupling due to increased vascular resistance.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed phenomenon based on physiological reasoning.

claim: Increased number of vessels synchronized in anti-phase during AngII infusion is supported by the increased vascular resistance, as predicted using mathematical modeling.
source: It is also supported by the increased number of vessels synchronized in anti-phase during the infusion, which, as we predicted using mathematical modeling (Postnov et al., 2012), is a natural consequence of stronger hemodynamic coupling.
evidence: This claim connects the experimental observation with prior modeling predictions.

claim: The direction of phase waves appears to be not predetermined by the vascular structure.
source: Interestingly, the direction of the phase waves appears to be not predetermined by the vascular structure - depending on the flow dynamics and other, yet unknown factors, it can change even within the same animal (an example is shown in Figure 4).
evidence: This is an observation from the phase wave analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: Phase wave behavior might be related to diffusive interaction between nephrons or the formation of synchronization centers (pacemakers) at different locations.
source: Such behavior might be related to diffusive interaction between nephrons or the formation of synchronization centers (pacemakers) at different locations.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed phase wave behavior.

claim: The presence of phase waves supports the deterministic nature of synchronization rather than random entrainment at the same dominant TGF frequency.
source: The presence of phase waves supports the deterministic nature of synchronization rather than random entrainment at the same dominant TGF frequency.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of synchronization based on the observation of phase waves.

claim: Similar phase wave effects are well studied in excitable media with diffusion interaction mechanisms such as brain and heart tissues.
source: Similar effects are well studied in excitable media with diffusion interaction mechanisms such as brain (Dahlem et al., 2010; Shibata and Bures, 1972) and heart (Alonso et al., 2016) tissues.
evidence: This claim draws on established knowledge from other biological systems, supported by citations.

claim: Such similarity might suggest the presence of a diffusive mechanism in the inter-nephron interaction or a long-distance fast electrical signaling, e.g., via conducted vasoreactivity.
source: Such similarity might suggest the presence of a diffusive mechanism in the inter-nephron interaction or a long-distance fast electrical signaling, e.g., via conducted vasoreactivity.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on comparison with other biological systems.

claim: Direct translation from individual segmented vessels to nephrons is challenging and requires further exploration.
source: While it provides an estimate of synchronization in the nephrons activity, direct translation from individual segmented vessels to nephrons is challenging and requires further exploration.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation in interpreting the data.

claim: LSCI can collect blood flow signal from as deep as 300–400 μm in theory.
source: While in theory, LSCI can collect the blood flow signal from as deep as 300–400 μm, in practice, visually resolvable signal typically comes from top 50 to 150 μm of the vascular structure (Davis et al., 2014; Zheng et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is based on theoretical understanding of LSCI technology.

claim: In practice, visually resolvable LSCI signal typically comes from top 50 to 150 μm of the vascular structure.
source: While in theory, LSCI can collect the blood flow signal from as deep as 300–400 μm, in practice, visually resolvable signal typically comes from top 50 to 150 μm of the vascular structure (Davis et al., 2014; Zheng et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies characterizing LSCI penetration depth.

claim: LSCI is likely limited to imaging vessels originating from ≈10000 nephrons in outer 30% of rat renal cortex.
source: Considering high vascular density close to the renal surface, it would mean that LSCI is likely limited to imaging vessels originating from ≈10000 nephrons in outer 30% of rat renal cortex (Letts et al., 2017), which would result in ≈40 nephrons in the 1.5 × 1.5 µm field of view.
evidence: This is an estimate based on anatomical knowledge and cited literature.

claim: This would result in ≈40 nephrons in the 1.5 × 1.5 µm field of view.
source: Considering high vascular density close to the renal surface, it would mean that LSCI is likely limited to imaging vessels originating from ≈10000 nephrons in outer 30% of rat renal cortex (Letts et al., 2017), which would result in ≈40 nephrons in the 1.5 × 1.5 µm field of view.
evidence: This is a calculation based on anatomical estimates.

claim: The larger number of segmented vessels can be explained by their mixed type - afferent and efferent arterioles as well as venules are likely to be segmented.
source: The larger number of segmented vessels can be explained by their mixed type - afferent and efferent arterioles as well as venules are likely to be segmented.
evidence: This is an explanation for the discrepancy between vessel count and nephron count based on vascular anatomy.

claim: Within the 1.5 × 1.5 µm field of view, we observe arterioles that arise from different non-terminal arteries.
source: When considering renal vascular topology, it is to be expected that within the 1.5 × 1.5 µm field of view, we observe arterioles that arise from different non-terminal arteries (Marsh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference based on knowledge of renal vascular anatomy, supported by citation.

claim: When a synchronous cluster is observed with LSCI, it is likely to extend several branching orders in depth and reach the size of hundreds and even thousands of nephrons.
source: Thus, when a synchronous cluster is observed with LSCI, it is likely to extend several branching orders in depth and reach the size of hundreds and even thousands of nephrons.
evidence: This is an inference about the actual size of synchronous clusters based on vascular topology.

claim: The exact role of inter-nephron communication, co-operative dynamics, and synchronization in kidney-related pathology development is still unclear and requires further exploration.
source: While the exact role of inter-nephron communication, co-operative dynamics, and synchronization in kidney-related pathology development is still unclear and requires further exploration, it is evidently altered by the blood pressure and vascular tone.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Inter-nephron communication is evidently altered by blood pressure and vascular tone.
source: While the exact role of inter-nephron communication, co-operative dynamics, and synchronization in kidney-related pathology development is still unclear and requires further exploration, it is evidently altered by the blood pressure and vascular tone.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental observations showing different synchronization patterns under different conditions.

claim: Strong local coupling and in-phase synchronization are likely to increase pressure variation at the level of afferent arterioles.
source: Strong local coupling and in-phase synchronization, while being not evident at the renal artery level (Postnov et al., 2015a), are likely to increase pressure variation at the level of afferent arterioles (Postnov et al., 2012; Postnov et al., 2016a), thus increasing chances of local damage and aggravating pathological condition.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to modeling studies and represents an inference about pathological consequences.

claim: Increased pressure variation at the level of afferent arterioles increases chances of local damage and aggravates pathological condition.
source: Strong local coupling and in-phase synchronization, while being not evident at the renal artery level (Postnov et al., 2015a), are likely to increase pressure variation at the level of afferent arterioles (Postnov et al., 2012; Postnov et al., 2016a), thus increasing chances of local damage and aggravating pathological condition.
evidence: This is an inference about pathological consequences based on the physiological effects of pressure variation.

claim: All experimental protocols were approved by the Danish National Animal Experiments Inspectorate (License 2015-15-0201-00463).
source: All experimental protocols were approved by the Danish National Animal Experiments Inspectorate (License 2015-15-0201-00463) and were conducted according to the American Physiological Society guidelines.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical approval for the experiments.

claim: Male Sprague Dawley rats with average weight ≈290 g (n = 5) were used.
source: Male Sprague Dawley rats (Taconic, Denmark) with average weight ≈290 g (n = 5) were used.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental subjects.

claim: Across all experiments, average arterial pressure was 112 ± 2 during control.
source: Across all experiments, average arterial pressure was 112 ± 2, 127 ± 6, and 100 ± 4 during the control, vasoconstrited (AngII), and vasodilated (ACh) conditions, respectively.
evidence: This is a measurement of arterial pressure during the control condition.

claim: Across all experiments, average arterial pressure was 127 ± 6 during vasoconstricted (AngII) condition.
source: Across all experiments, average arterial pressure was 112 ± 2, 127 ± 6, and 100 ± 4 during the control, vasoconstrited (AngII), and vasodilated (ACh) conditions, respectively.
evidence: This is a measurement of arterial pressure during AngII infusion.

claim: Across all experiments, average arterial pressure was 100 ± 4 during vasodilated (ACh) condition.
source: Across all experiments, average arterial pressure was 112 ± 2, 127 ± 6, and 100 ± 4 during the control, vasoconstrited (AngII), and vasodilated (ACh) conditions, respectively.
evidence: This is a measurement of arterial pressure during ACh infusion.

claim: A single-mode fiber-coupled laser diode (785 nm) was used to deliver coherent light onto kidney surface with a power density of approximately 10 mW/cm².
source: A single-mode fiber-coupled laser diode (785 nm, LP785-SF100, Thorlabs, USA) controlled with a laser driver and temperature controller (CLD1011LP, Thorlabs, USA) was used to deliver coherent light onto kidney surface with a power density of approximately 10 mW/cm2, providing an optimal signal-to-noise ratio (Postnov et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is a description of the imaging system specifications.

claim: Exposure time was set to 5 ms, which provides optimal sensitivity to slow flows, such as in capillary perfused tissue.
source: Exposure time was set to 5 ms, which provides optimal sensitivity to slow flows, such as in capillary perfused tissue (Yuan et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a methodological choice supported by citation to prior work on LSCI optimization.

claim: The system provides an image resolution of 2.25 µm²/px compared with previously published studies on renal synchronization, which used the system with the image resolution of 45–400 µm²/px.
source: The system provides an image resolution of 2.25 µm2/px compared with previously published studies on renal synchronization, which used the system with the image resolution of 45–400 µm2/px (Holstein-Rathlou et al., 2011; Scully et al., 2013; Mitrou et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison of the current system's capabilities with prior systems, supported by citations.

claim: The system has a higher temporal resolution (50 fps instead of 25) compared to previous studies.
source: Similarly, the system has a higher temporal resolution (50 fps instead of 25) and utilizes a better light source (Postnov et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is a comparison of temporal resolution with prior systems.

claim: These factors improve the expected signal-to-noise ratio per area unit by at least 30 times.
source: Combined and considering noise reduction achieved by spatial and temporal averaging, these factors improve the expected signal-to-noise ratio per area unit by at least 30 times.
evidence: This is a calculation of the improvement in signal-to-noise ratio based on the system specifications.

claim: Continuous wavelet transform analysis (Morse wavelet) was applied to segmented vessels' BFI to identify the frequency and phase of dominant periodic activity in the 0.015–0.05 Hz frequency band associated with the TGF mechanism.
source: To study synchronization patterns between microcirculatory vessels and, thus, obtain insight into inter-nephron communication, we apply continuous wavelet transform analysis (Morse wavelet, MATLAB) to segmented vessels' BFI. We identified the frequency and phase of dominant periodic activity in the 0.015–0.05 Hz frequency band associated with the TGF mechanism.
evidence: This is a description of the analysis method used to study synchronization.

claim: Blood flow in different segmented vessels is considered to be synchronized whenever their dominant frequencies match.
source: In this study, we consider blood flow in different segmented vessels to be synchronized whenever their dominant frequencies match.
evidence: This is a definition of the synchronization criterion used in the study.

claim: Paired t-test was applied to compare results between control, AngII infusion, and ACh infusion.
source: Paired t-test was applied to compare results between control, AngII infusion, and ACh infusion.
evidence: This is a description of the statistical method used.

claim: p-values greater than 0.05 are reported as not significant.
source: p-values greater than 0.05 are reported as not significant.
evidence: This is a statement of the statistical significance threshold used.
